title: Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage: SNF Advance Beneficiary Notice
content:
**Rule.** Before extended care that Medicare is not expected to cover is billed to the resident, such as skilled care the center keeps providing after the last covered date of a NOMNC, the SNF Advance Beneficiary Notice is delivered and the beneficiary checks one of its three options; the choice is the beneficiary's own and is recorded exactly as checked. Option 1 keeps the care going and obliges the center to submit a demand bill to Medicare; the resident pays while the claim is pending and is refunded if Medicare pays. Option 2 keeps the care going with no claim to Medicare, and the resident pays. Option 3 stops the non-covered care, and nothing is billed for it. Without a delivered SNF ABN the center may not bill the resident for that care. No SNF ABN is needed when coverage ends because the benefit-period day limit is reached. One notice is recorded per delivery date and first non-covered date.

The SNF ABN (CMS-10055) is the Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage notice for care Medicare is not expected to cover.

| Option checked | Care | Claim to Medicare | Who pays |
|---|---|---|---|
| Option 1 — bill Medicare | Continues | Demand bill submitted by the center | The resident, while the claim is pending; refunded if Medicare pays |
| Option 2 — no bill | Continues | None | The resident |
| Option 3 — stop services | Stops | None | Nothing is billed for that care |

| SNF ABN delivered | The resident may be billed for the non-covered care |
|---|---|
| Yes | As the checked option provides |
| No | No |
